channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Brasil aparece pouco em newsletter dos EUA sobre noticiário internacional
item.description: The U.S.-based Semafor Flagship newsletter mentioned Brazil in only 10 of over 100 daily editions from January to May 2026, reflecting limited international coverage. Mentions included Wagner Moura’s Oscar nomination, the invasive golden mussel in the Amazon, Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential pre-candidacy announcement, Embraer’s record order backlog, the overturning of Lula’s veto on the dosimetry bill, and a Lula-Trump meeting. Despite some topics gaining national traction, international attention remained sparse and often tied to U.S. interests or domestic political controversies.

item.title: Polarizaram a seleção brasileira
item.description: On the eve of Brazil's opening match against Morocco in the World Cup, political polarization intensified. The PT launched the campaign 'Lula plays for Brazil,' seeking to link support for the former president to the defense of national sovereignty during the tournament.

item.title: PT critica Tarcísio por free flow, mas governo Lula também adota modelo em rodoviais federais
item.description: The PT criticizes Governor Tarcísio de Freitas for the chaotic implementation of free-flow tolling in São Paulo, citing lack of transparency and communication to drivers. However, Tarcísio’s allies note that the model was expanded under President Lula’s administration on federal highways, with ANTT authorizing electronic tolling in seven concessions. The state government denies electoral motives, claiming a technical and gradual strategy, despite postponements and cancellations of toll gantries due to public complaints.

item.title: Veja a programação das melhores rodas de samba do Rio neste fim de semana de jogo do Brasil na Copa do Mundo
item.description: This weekend in Rio de Janeiro combines the broadcast of Brazil’s World Cup debut with a diverse schedule of samba circles, including free and paid performances across neighborhoods such as Realengo, Lapa, Centro and Penha. Highlights include Terreiro de Crioulo at Sesc Nova Iguaçu, Arlindinho das Antigas at Beco do Rato and Arena Senado with LED screens for watching the match, plus attractions like Mal de Raiz, Quintal da Magia and Samba D'Coroa.

item.title: Geração 'pós-penta' é a mais empolgada com a Copa do Mundo, mas queda de otimismo no Brasil liga alerta
item.description: The generation born after Brazil’s fifth World Cup win (2002) shows the highest optimism for a sixth title in 2026, yet confidence among Brazilians aged 16–24 has dropped sharply—from 63% in July 2022 to 35% in April 2026, per Datafolha. While individuals like Bernardo Durães and Alice Fernandes express hope, prolonged team underperformance and traumatic memories such as the 7–1 loss to Germany in 2014 have weakened collective faith, despite perceptions of increased commitment from the current squad.

item.title: Passado de glórias e histórico de craques do Brasil provocam fascínio nos motoristas de aplicativo em Los Angeles
item.description: The text describes how ride-share drivers in Los Angeles, many of whom are immigrants from the Global South, express deep admiration for the Brazilian national football team, particularly legends like Ronaldinho, Ronaldo, Rivaldo, and Kaká. This admiration extends beyond sports, touching on cultural ties such as the large Lebanese community in São Paulo, and becomes a meaningful point of human connection amidst LA’s chaotic traffic.

item.title: Após revés na COP30, Brasil flexibiliza 'mapa do caminho' para atrair apoio à redução do uso de combustíveis fósseis
item.description: Brazil signaled that its global 'roadmap' for phasing out fossil fuels will be flexible after its proposal was excluded from the COP30 final text due to resistance from petrostates like Saudi Arabia, India, and Russia. The Lula administration aims to formally present the roadmap at COP31 in Turkey, despite domestic delays and criticism that the setback undermines Lula's international credibility on climate leadership.

item.title: Presidente do PT diz que caso 'Dark Horse' pode ampliar impacto eleitoral sobre bolsonarismo
item.description: PT national president Edinho Silva says the 'Dark Horse' case, involving Banco Master's financing of the film, could politically damage Bolsonaro's camp if investigations progress, citing the proven closeness between Flávio Bolsonaro and businessman Daniel Vorcaro. He believes Flávio may retain part of his base but argues this doesn't equate to national electoral strength, emphasizing that bolsonarism has social force but not necessarily the capacity to win broad national projects.

item.title: Decisão que liberou Zambelli na Itália fala em 'dupla condição' e falta de imparcialidade de Moraes; veja próximos passos
item.description: Italy's Court of Cassation denied the extradition of former deputy Carla Zambelli to Brazil, stating that Minister Alexandre de Moraes acted as 'victim, witness, and judge' in the case, creating a 'dual condition' that undermines impartiality. The ruling is based on the 1989 Brazil-Italy extradition treaty, which bars surrender when there are doubts about respect for minimum defense rights. Zambelli was sentenced to 10 years in prison by Brazil's STF for being the intellectual author of the invasion of the National Justice Council (CNJ) system, with support from hacker Walter Delgatti Neto.

item.title: Sem palanque, Flávio Bolsonaro enfrenta desafio na Bahia, e PL racha sobre apoio à campanha de ACM Neto
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro faces resistance within the Bahia PL due to the lack of formal support from ACM Neto, who has aligned with Ronaldo Caiado in the first round. A faction of the PL pushes for early support for Flávio given his struggle to build Northeastern slates, while another faction argues that right-wing backing for ACM Neto is not automatic and requires dialogue. The split highlights internal party conflict and an added challenge for the senator in a state where Lula and the PT dominate.

item.title: 'Paradoxo da direita': Flávio Bolsonaro perde força, mas rivais não conseguem herdar votos anti-Lula, diz diretor da Quaest
item.description: The June 2026 Quaest poll reveals a paradox in Brazil's right-wing: although Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) is losing ground due to the Banco Master scandal and improved perception of Lula's government, no center-right or alternative right-wing candidate has managed to consistently capitalize on his decline. Lula leads with 39% in the first-round vote intention, followed by Flávio at 29%, while all other opposition candidates combined reach only 12%, indicating a fragmented and polarized race with no viable third way emerging.

item.title: Eleições 2026: Novo tenta se equilibrar entre candidatura de Zema e alianças com Flávio Bolsonaro nos estados
item.description: The Novo party aims to position itself as a right-wing alternative to Bolsonarism with Romeu Zema’s 2026 presidential bid, yet maintains strategic alliances with Flávio Bolsonaro’s PL in states to overcome the electoral threshold and access public funding. With over R$ 37 million from the Electoral Fund and nearly R$ 100 million accumulated since 2018, the party plans to field complete slates in most states, building on its municipal success in 2024, when it grew from 35 to 264 councilors and from 1 to 19 mayors.

item.title: De Pelé a Neymar: como futebol e política no Brasil se cruzam nas Copas do Mundo
item.description: Neymar's call-up to the Brazilian national team sparked political intersections, as the Liberal Party used AI to associate him with senator Flávio Bolsonaro, a 2026 presidential pre-candidate. While Lula praised the team's potential to win a sixth World Cup, he lamented the lack of current football idols and joked with Trump about visas for the 2026 Cup. Experts note that World Cup years in Brazil have coincided with elections since 1994, amplifying the political impact of athletes' actions.

item.title: Em novo vídeo, Flávio critica Lula e PT por uso da camisa da seleção
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro released a pre-campaign video criticizing Lula and the PT for wearing Brazil's national team jersey only during elections and World Cups, while his supporters wear it 'all their lives'. The video, featuring a sertanejo jingle titled 'Vem com Fé', emphasizes hope, trust in the future, and popular participation, using Brazil's flag colors and showing the senator in pre-campaign activities.

item.title: Defensoria pede adiamento de julgamento de Eduardo Bolsonaro no STF
item.description: The General Public Defender's Office requested the postponement of the trial against Eduardo Bolsonaro at the STF, arguing that the First Chamber has been incomplete for eight months due to the vacancy left by Justice Luís Roberto Barroso's retirement. The DPU warns that a four-judge panel could result in a 2-2 tie, and if relator Alexandre de Moraes is recused, only three judges would remain, undermining the decision's validity. It urges the invocation of a minister from the Second Chamber under Article 41 of the STF's Internal Regulations to ensure a proper quorum.

item.title: Gonet anuncia vigilância da PGR contra deepfakes e facções na campanha eleitoral
item.description: Attorney General Paulo Gonet announced the PGR's immediate vigilance against deepfakes and criminal faction interference in the 2026 elections, noting the difficulty in distinguishing malicious AI-generated content from legitimate material and warning of militias blocking campaigns in territories under their control. He also criticized the excessive judicialization of social conflicts and the STF's role as a third chamber of Congress, while affirming the PGR's independence from political pressures.

item.title: Fachin cria três frentes de ação para reformar o Judiciário e busca agregar colegas à proposta
item.description: Supreme Court President Edson Fachin has launched three reform fronts for the Judiciary: a Code of Ethics, a remuneration system, and a working group for judicial modernization, seeking collegial input to avoid internal opposition. The initiative aims to restore public trust damaged by scandals like the Banco Master case and position judicial reform as a central electoral issue in 2026.

item.title: “Trump escuta [Lula] e fica todo animado”, garante Durigan
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan warned that the continuous growth of mandatory spending poses a structural risk to Brazil's public finances, stating that without moderation, the country could become fiscally unviable. He emphasized that unchecked increases in these expenses compress the sustainability limit.

item.title: O ‘problemão’ que aguarda o vencedor da eleição presidencial de 2026
item.description: The next Brazilian president, to be elected in 2026, will inherit a more difficult fiscal scenario and will need to implement a tougher adjustment starting in 2027 to reorganize public accounts and contain debt, regardless of the election outcome. According to André Roncaglia, executive director for Brazil at the IMF, while the current government seeks to preserve fiscal credibility and address social demands, the burden of restructuring will fall on the next administration, requiring political negotiation among branches and measures such as flexibility in mandatory spending and gradual reduction of tax exemptions.

item.title: Zema volta a criticar Flávio Bolsonaro por relação com Vorcaro e diz que Bolsa Família 'forma geração de imprestáveis'
item.description: Presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema (Novo) renewed his criticism of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) over his ties to banker Daniel Vorcaro, calling him a 'criminal' and stating that those who associate with him should be viewed with caution. Zema also attacked the Bolsa Família program, claiming it 'forms a generation of the useless' by discouraging work. Despite the critiques, he left open the possibility of an alliance with Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) in a runoff, while maintaining separate candidacies in the first round.

item.title: Produtora declara gasto de R$ 75 mi com filme sobre Bolsonaro, diz jornal
item.description: Go Up Entertainment declared in judicial expertise having spent R$ 75 million on the production of "Dark Horse", a film about former President Jair Bolsonaro, with R$ 54.2 million spent in the U.S. and R$ 20.9 million in Brazil. The declaration is part of a legal case investigating the ICB for suspected misappropriation of São Paulo city funds to finance the film, whose initial approved budget was US$ 16 million. The expertise confirmed the financial resources originated from private sources, supported by investment contracts and banking records.

item.title: Caiado prevê agenda com Renan Santos: "Muita coisa para atualizar"
item.description: Presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) said he plans to schedule a meeting with Renan Santos (Mission) to update their political alignment, recalling their long-standing partnership since the Dilma Rousseff impeachment. Caiado praised Renan for founding his own party and said the conversation will be productive, as both are open to dialogue for a potential presidential ticket. A Quaest poll showed a technical tie between the two at 3% in voter intentions.

item.title: Mendonça pede posição da PGR sobre transferência de Vorcaro
item.description: Supreme Court Justice André Mendonça has requested the Attorney General's Office to state its position on transferring former banker Daniel Vorcaro to a regular prison, after the Federal Police rejected his second plea bargain proposal. Vorcaro has been in preventive detention since March 19, 2026, at the PF Superintendency in Brasília, under investigation in Operation Compliance Zero for alleged fraud at Banco Master. No response has been received from the PGR or the defense as of publication.

item.title: Facções criminosas ameaçam integridade das eleições, diz Gonet
item.description: Attorney General Paulo Gonet identified the activities of criminal organizations as one of the main challenges to electoral integrity in the 2026 elections. He announced that the Federal Public Ministry will prioritize combating interference by these groups in the electoral process. The statement was made in an interview with EsferaCast, a videocast by Esfera Brasil.

item.title: Petrobras deve assinar memorando com Pemex neste mês, diz Magda
item.description: Petrobras president Magda Chambriard announced that Pemex’s president will visit Brazil this month to sign a memorandum of understanding and confidentiality agreements, launching joint studies in technology, exploration, production, and refining. The cooperation follows talks between Lula and Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum and aims to explore potential business opportunities amid rising Asian demand for oil due to Middle East tensions. Chambriard also noted the first sale of green coke to Saudi Aramco in China and addressed a fiscal dispute with the Rio de Janeiro government over an alleged R$ 20 billion credit.

item.title: A ‘piora considerável’ na saúde de Jair Bolsonaro, segundo médico
item.description: Former President Jair Bolsonaro experienced a significant deterioration in his health following a medication change, leading to increased hiccup crises and the need for extra doses of medication at the therapeutic safety limit. His doctor recommends new digestive exams, such as an endoscopy, to adjust treatment. The situation arises just before the STF re-evaluates his house arrest, with the current 90-day period ending on March 25.

item.title: Lula diz que eleitores devem “dar cacete” por promessas não cumpridas
item.description: President Lula stated that voters should demand the fulfillment of campaign promises and act as government overseers, using the phrase 'dar cacete' to pressure for concrete actions. He emphasized that poor populations are often ignored outside election periods and defended the expansion of the Minha Casa, Minha Vida program with R$10 billion for 85,000 housing units, linking the lack of income circulation to persistent poverty and inequality in Brazil.

item.title: TSE institui grupo que vai criar plano para uso de IA na Justiça Eleitoral
item.description: The TSE has established a permanent committee to organize, regulate, and plan the use of artificial intelligence within the Electoral Justice system, focusing on countering disinformation and the spread of fake news. The committee will also set ethical guidelines, define procurement requirements, create a national catalog of AI solutions, and monitor agreements with universities and entities specializing in digital forensics and AI, in line with the updated electoral propaganda resolution of 2024.

item.title: Pogba surpreende e diz que França atual é melhor que a campeã de 2018
item.description: Paul Pogba stated that the current French national team is stronger than the 2018 World Cup champions and even the 2022 squad in terms of individual talent, though he noted that winning a World Cup requires more than just skill. He identified Brazil, Portugal, and Spain as serious contenders, suggesting Brazil could be a major surprise in the 2026 tournament.

item.title: “Zambelli se sentiu culpada”, diz advogado sobre derrota de Bolsonaro
item.description: Lawyer Fábio Pagnozzi, part of Carla Zambelli’s defense team, said she felt responsible for Jair Bolsonaro’s defeat in the 2022 elections. Zambelli was sentenced by the STF to five years and three months in semi-open prison for illegal firearm possession and other offenses. The statement was made in an interview on Friday, April 12.

item.title: Governo Lula entrega 85.000 moradias do Minha Casa, Minha Vida
item.description: President Lula’s government announced the selection of 85,000 housing units under the Minha Casa, Minha Vida program — 50,000 for rural areas and 35,000 for the Entities modality — with a R$ 10 billion investment from the Social Development Fund, exceeding the 2025 target. Lula denounced income inequality and praised the program as a tool for social inclusion, while Minister Guilherme Boulos contrasted it with Bolsonaro’s Casa Verde e Amarela, claiming the latter failed to deliver meaningful housing.

item.title: Clica e Confirma: serviços ampliam o acesso da população à Justiça Eleitoral
item.description: The Clica e Confirma program highlights TSE initiatives to expand access to the Electoral Justice, including a partnership with public defenders to provide free legal assistance to economically vulnerable candidates and voters. It also covers the creation of Working Groups on indigenous and Black inclusion, AI use, cybersecurity, and social media norms, as well as the Senate's inspection of the source code of electronic voting machines.

item.title: Moraes autoriza visitas de aliados de Bolsonaro a Braga Netto na prisão
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes authorized 17 visits by allies of former President Jair Bolsonaro to General Walter Braga Netto, who is imprisoned for an attempted coup. Among those authorized are PL Senate leader Carlos Portinho and other party members and former Bolsonaro ministers.

item.title: Caiado elogia Renan Santos e fala em 'sentar e conversar' em meio a especulações sobre escolha de vice
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado praised Renan Santos during a PSD event in Botucatu (SP) and said he intends to 'sit down and talk' with him to update agendas and strengthen political dialogue. The remarks come amid speculation about a possible presidential ticket, following a Quaest poll showing a technical tie between the two at 3% in voter intentions. Caiado highlighted Renan’s trajectory, mentioning his role in the Dilma impeachment mobilization and his political articulation skills.

item.title: 39% atribuem sucesso do Pix ao BC, diz pesquisa
item.description: A Real Time Big Data survey shows 39% of Brazilians credit the Central Bank for Pix’s success, followed by 23% attributing it to Jair Bolsonaro and 16% to Lula. Despite U.S. criticism — including threats of 25% tariffs and claims that Pix constitutes unfair trade practices — 96% of users approve the system. 41% believe Trump could end Pix in Brazil, while 49% see no risk of its discontinuation even if Lula is not re-elected.

item.title: Lula finaliza radioterapia contra câncer de pele
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva completed his final radiotherapy session on Friday at the Sírio-Libanês Hospital to treat an early-stage skin cancer on his scalp. The treatment consisted of 15 two-minute sessions over two weeks, administered as a preventive measure following the removal of a small lesion. During a public event announcing a new credit line for app-based delivery workers, Lula reassured the public that he is doing well after concluding the therapy.

item.title: Augusto Nardes antecipa aposentadoria do TCU por motivos de saúde
item.description: TCU Minister Augusto Nardes announced an early retirement in December due to health reasons, opening a seat from the Chamber of Deputies' quota. His departure occurs ten months before his mandatory retirement in 2027 and is expected to trigger a political dispute over his replacement, with House President Hugo Motta leading the negotiations. The vacancy follows the linked appointment rule, meaning it must be filled by the same entity that appointed the previous minister.

item.title: A fronteira esburacada da ética pública
item.description: The text criticizes patrimonialism in Brazil, highlighting the persistent fusion of public and private assets as a colonial legacy, manifested in the misuse of state resources — such as FAB aircraft for personal or partisan purposes — and budgetary capture through parliamentary earmarks and the appointment of public officials to paid positions in private or mixed-economy companies, thereby circumventing public sector remuneration limits.

item.title: TSE normalizou a censura sob as regras do direito xandônico
item.description: The text criticizes the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) for normalizing censorship under the guise of combating disinformation, citing the prior banning of a film in 2022 and the suspension of an electoral poll by Minister Nunes Marques, who invoked the vague concept of 'captiousness' to invalidate questions about the Master scheme. It argues that while such measures were initially praised as defending democracy, they establish an authoritarian precedent that can be exploited by any authority to suppress free speech and public debate, including on politically significant issues like the Master scheme’s influence on voter perceptions.

item.title: “Fui ao PP com a condição de apoiar incondicionalmente Flávio”, diz Derrite
item.description: Federal deputy Guilherme Derrite (PP) stated he joined the Progressistas party on the condition of unconditionally supporting Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) in his 2026 presidential bid. He emphasized that forming the Senate ticket sooner would be better for the campaign. The remarks were made in an interview with CNN on Friday, the 12th.

item.title: Colégio de Presidentes dos TREs elege nova liderança nacional
item.description: Catarinian judge Carlos Roberto da Silva was elected president of the Collegiate of Presidents of Regional Electoral Courts (Coptrel) by acclamation during the entity's 91st meeting in Florianópolis. He has presided over the TRE-SC since March 2026 and has extensive experience in electoral justice, having joined the judiciary in 1993 and been promoted to a judge of the TJSC in 2019. Coptrel brings together state electoral court presidents to discuss guidelines and coordinate strategic actions for the improvement of Brazil's Electoral Justice.

item.title: A irritação da bancada ruralista com atuação de ministro da Agricultura de Lula
item.description: The ruralist caucus expressed irritation with Agriculture Minister André de Paula following a meeting with the Parliamentary Agricultural Front (FPA), claiming he lacks sector knowledge, political will, and fails to address critical issues such as debt, EU trade barriers, and the 2026/2027 Harvest Plan.

item.title: Maioria dos usuários no Brasil já confundiu deepfake com realidade, aponta pesquisa inédita
item.description: An unprecedented study shows 70.2% of Brazilian internet users have mistaken deepfakes for real content, revealing high susceptibility to digital fraud and disinformation. Less than one-fifth (18.7%) feel confident in immediately identifying deepfakes, while only 39.3% regularly verify AI chatbot responses. In 2026, deepfakes featuring Lula and fabricated police violence are rising, amplifying electoral and security risks.

item.title: Planalto quer evitar embate com Trump em discurso de Lula no G7
item.description: The Lula administration aims to avoid a direct confrontation with the U.S. at the G7, pursuing a diplomatic tone and advocating for multilateral trade rules without directly referencing U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods. Negotiations are being handled through technical channels, and no bilateral meeting between Lula and Trump is expected during the summit.

item.title: Lula se diz curado do câncer de pele ao anunciar conclusão de radioterapia
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva announced the completion of 15 radiotherapy sessions to treat skin cancer, declaring himself cured. The treatment followed the removal of a basal cell carcinoma on his head in April and was conducted daily at the Sírio-Libanês Hospital. Although full remission requires five years without symptoms, doctors note that this type of cancer has a high cure rate.

item.title: 96% dos brasileiros aprovam o Pix, afirma pesquisa
item.description: A Real Time Big Data survey released on June 12, 2026, shows that 96% of the 78% of Brazilians who have used Pix approve of the payment service, with a 3-point margin of error and 95% confidence level. The approval comes amid U.S. criticism, which proposed a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods after the USTR cited Pix as an unfair trade practice. Despite this, 48% of respondents view Lula’s defense of Pix as correct due to national sovereignty, while 42% see it as opportunistic and election-driven.

item.title: Entenda como a CPMI do Master foi parar na gaveta do Congresso, sob gestão de Alcolumbre
item.description: Congress President Davi Alcolumbre resisted installing the CPMI on Banco Master despite over 280 signatures meeting the regulatory quorum, stating that reading the requests is a discretionary act of the presidency. Allies suggest his resistance stems from avoiding initiatives that could influence the 2026 elections. The allegation that Alcolumbre received $30 million from Banco Master owner Daniel Vorcaro, disclosed in a plea deal, was cited by pre-candidate Romeu Zema as the reason for blocking the investigation, although Alcolumbre denied receiving any funds.

item.title: Acabou a química? Lula vai ao G7 sem agenda com Trump
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva traveled to the G7 summit in France without a scheduled bilateral meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump. Neither side requested or signaled interest in such a meeting, indicating a cooling in bilateral relations. The lack of agenda raises questions about the state of the 'chemistry' between the two leaders.

item.title: Zelensky e autoridades árabes vão discutir guerras na cúpula do G7
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky will attend the G7 summit in Évian-les-Bains, France, to discuss the war in Ukraine, international support, and long-term commitments. Arab leaders from Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and the UAE will also participate to address the conflict between the U.S., Israel, and Iran, focusing on the Strait of Hormuz and the global energy crisis. Brazil, as a guest country, will be represented by President Lula, though no meeting with Trump is expected.

item.title: "Não revelei segredos de Estado", diz Aldo Rebelo sobre ET de Varginha
item.description: Former Defense Minister Aldo Rebelo denied revealing state secrets regarding the Varginha UFO incident, stating his comments about a supposed extraterrestrial sighting in 1996 were based solely on publicly available information, including press reports and testimonies from doctors and military personnel. He emphasized he had no access to classified Defense Ministry data and advocated for international transparency, suggesting Brazil should follow the U.S. if it declassifies UAP documents. His remarks sparked controversy, with science communicator Sérgio Sacani demanding clarification if the claims have any basis in fact.
